name: org.machanism.machai:project-layout
description: Project Layout is a Java utility library for describing, detecting, and working with conventional project directory layouts in a consistent way. It provides a shared model for locating well-known folders such as production sources, test sources, resources, and documentation directories across heterogeneous repositories and build ecosystems. Instead of duplicating path conventions throughout each tool, Project Layout centralizes these rules behind reusable layout implementations, improving maintainability, reducing configuration drift, and making project-structure discovery easier to adapt across different technology stacks and repository styles. The library defines the abstract base class org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout and concrete ecosystem-specific strategies: MavenProjectLayout (reads pom.xml build metadata via PomReader for modules, source, test, resource, and documentation directories), GradleProjectLayout (uses the Gradle Tooling API to load the GradleProject model and expose conventional src/main, src/test, and src/site roots), JScriptProjectLayout (resolves JavaScript/TypeScript workspace modules from package.json), PythonProjectLayout (detects Python projects from pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg, requirements.txt, and Pipfile), and DefaultProjectLayout (a lightweight fallback that treats each immediate subdirectory as a module). The org.machanism.machai.project package provides ProjectLayoutManager for automatic layout detection through detectProjectLayout(File) and the abstract ProjectProcessor base class for recursively scanning project roots and nested modules. Layout accessors return root-relative paths using a forward slash separator, resolved against the configured project directory. The library is ideal for build plugins, repository scanners, code generators, documentation tooling, validation workflows, and project indexing. It is a lightweight, pure Java library built with Maven, targeting Java 8 or later, and integrates SLF4J for logging, Jackson for JSON parsing, Apache Commons IO and Commons Lang3 utilities, TOMLJ for TOML parsing, the Gradle Tooling API, and the Apache Maven model libraries.

constructors.description: Creates a Maven-specific ProjectLayout instance. After construction, the project root must be configured with projectDir(java.io.File) before invoking layout accessors. Reads Maven build metadata from pom.xml to determine modules (when packaging is pom), source and resource directories, test source and resource directories, and documentation inputs (default src/site).

examples.description: Instantiates a MavenProjectLayout, configures the project root directory, and reads the source and resource directories derived from the project's pom.xml.

constructors.description: Creates a Gradle-specific ProjectLayout instance. It uses the Gradle Tooling API to load a GradleProject model (cached after loading) and exposes module names, conventional source roots (src/main), test roots (src/test), and documentation inputs (src/site). The project root must be configured with projectDir(java.io.File) before use.

examples.description: Creates a GradleProjectLayout, sets the project directory, and retrieves the list of child module names for a multi-project Gradle build.

constructors.description: Creates a minimal fallback ProjectLayout instance. This layout performs a lightweight filesystem inspection and treats each immediate subdirectory of the configured project root as a potential module, excluding entries listed in ProjectLayout.getExcludeDirs(). It does not infer language-specific source, test, or documentation roots.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.project.layout.DefaultProjectLayout layout = new org.machanism.machai.project.layout.DefaultProjectLayout();
java.util.List<java.lang.String> modules = layout.projectDir(new java.io.File("C:\\repo")).getModules();
examples.description: Creates a DefaultProjectLayout as a fallback and lists immediate subdirectories of the project root as modules.

constructors.description: Creates a PomReader instance for reading and processing Maven pom.xml files into Maven models. Provides model parsing (with property substitution), property collection, and model serialization to XML.

examples.description: Creates a PomReader, parses a pom.xml into a Maven Model, and reads the collected POM properties.

features.name: detectProjectLayout
features.signature: public static org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout detectProjectLayout(java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.FileNotFoundException
features.description: Detects and instantiates the appropriate ProjectLayout implementation based on the contents of the specified project directory. Supports Maven, Node.js (package.json), and Python projects, defaulting to a generic DefaultProjectLayout when no supported project type is detected. Throws FileNotFoundException if the project directory does not exist.

examples.description: Automatically detects the project layout for a directory and reads its conventional source directories without hard-coding ecosystem-specific rules.

features.name: scanFolder
features.signature: public void scanFolder(java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Scans the main project directory, detects modules, and processes them. If modules are present, each module is processed recursively; otherwise the entire folder structure is processed. Concrete folder handling is delegated to subclasses of the abstract ProjectProcessor via processFolder(ProjectLayout).

examples.description: Implements a custom ProjectProcessor and scans a project directory, processing each detected module or the whole folder structure.

features.name: getSources
features.description: Returns the root-relative source directories for production code. Implementations resolve these from build metadata or conventions. MavenProjectLayout inspects the Maven build section (applying Maven defaults when undefined) and returns a Set; GradleProjectLayout returns src/main; DefaultProjectLayout, JScriptProjectLayout, and PythonProjectLayout return empty lists.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout layout = new org.machanism.machai.project.layout.MavenProjectLayout().projectDir(new java.io.File("C:\\repo"));
java.util.Collection<java.lang.String> sources = layout.getSources();
examples.description: Resolves the root-relative production source directories from a Maven project's pom.xml build section.

features.name: getTests
features.description: Returns the root-relative source directories for test code. MavenProjectLayout returns test source and test resource directories from the build section; GradleProjectLayout returns src/test; DefaultProjectLayout, JScriptProjectLayout, and PythonProjectLayout return empty lists.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout layout = new org.machanism.machai.project.layout.GradleProjectLayout().projectDir(new java.io.File("C:\\gradle-repo"));
java.util.Collection<java.lang.String> tests = layout.getTests();
examples.description: Retrieves the conventional test source directories (src/test) for a Gradle project.

features.name: getDocuments
features.description: Returns the root-relative documentation directories. MavenProjectLayout and GradleProjectLayout return src/site; DefaultProjectLayout, JScriptProjectLayout, and PythonProjectLayout return empty lists.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout layout = new org.machanism.machai.project.layout.MavenProjectLayout().projectDir(new java.io.File("C:\\repo"));
java.util.Collection<java.lang.String> docs = layout.getDocuments();
examples.description: Resolves the documentation directories (src/site) for a Maven project.

features.name: getModules
features.description: Returns a list of module directories or names within the project, or null for non-parent projects (in the base contract). MavenProjectLayout returns declared pom.xml modules when packaging is pom; GradleProjectLayout returns child project names for multi-project builds; JScriptProjectLayout returns workspace modules from package.json; DefaultProjectLayout returns each immediate subdirectory (never null).

examples.description: Retrieves the module directories declared in a multi-module Maven project's pom.xml.

features.name: isMavenProject
features.description: Checks whether the given directory appears to be a Maven project by verifying the presence of a pom.xml file. Returns true if pom.xml exists in the directory; false otherwise.

examples.snippet: boolean isMaven = org.machanism.machai.project.layout.MavenProjectLayout.isMavenProject(new java.io.File("C:\\repo"));
examples.description: Determines whether a directory is a Maven project by detecting a pom.xml file.

features.name: isGradleProject
features.description: Checks whether the given directory appears to be a Gradle project by verifying the presence of a build.gradle file. Returns true if build.gradle exists in the directory; false otherwise.

examples.snippet: boolean isGradle = org.machanism.machai.project.layout.GradleProjectLayout.isGradleProject(new java.io.File("C:\\gradle-repo"));
examples.description: Determines whether a directory is a Gradle project by detecting a build.gradle file.

features.name: isPackageJsonPresent
features.description: Checks if the specified directory contains a package.json file, indicating a JavaScript/TypeScript project. Returns true if package.json is present; otherwise false.

examples.snippet: boolean isJs = org.machanism.machai.project.layout.JScriptProjectLayout.isPackageJsonPresent(new java.io.File("C:\\js-repo"));
examples.description: Determines whether a directory is a JavaScript/TypeScript project by detecting a package.json file.

features.name: isPythonProject
features.description: Checks whether the provided directory is a Python project. Looks for pyproject.toml, setup.py, or setup.cfg; checks for requirements.txt, Pipfile, or typical virtual environment directories; and examines Python file structures and project classifiers. Returns true if a Python project is detected, false otherwise.

examples.snippet: boolean isPython = org.machanism.machai.project.layout.PythonProjectLayout.isPythonProject(new java.io.File("C:\\py-repo"));
examples.description: Determines whether a directory is a Python project by inspecting metadata and dependency files.

features.name: getRelativePath
features.signature: public static java.lang.String getRelativePath(java.io.File dir, java.io.File file, boolean addSingleDot)
features.description: Computes the relative path from the specified project directory to the target file. Optionally prefixes the result with './' when addSingleDot is true. Returns '.' if the target file is the same as the project directory, or null if the target file is not within the project directory.

examples.snippet: java.lang.String rel = org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout.getRelativePath(new java.io.File("C:\\repo"), new java.io.File("C:\\repo\\src\\main\\java"), true);
examples.description: Computes the root-relative path './src/main/java' of a nested file relative to the project directory.

features.name: getProjectModel
features.description: Loads and returns the Maven model from a pom.xml file. Performs a lightweight parse of the POM after applying property substitutions. Throws IllegalArgumentException if the pom.xml cannot be processed.

examples.description: Parses a pom.xml file into a Maven Model and reads the artifactId.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout
studs.description: Base abstraction for describing a project's conventional on-disk layout. Translates build tool conventions and/or build metadata into root-relative paths such as source roots, test roots, documentation roots, and optionally module directories. Implementations must be configured with a project root via projectDir(java.io.File) before accessors are called. Extend this class to add support for new build ecosystems.

examples.description: Defines a custom layout for a new ecosystem by extending ProjectLayout and implementing the abstract source, test, and documentation accessors.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.project.ProjectProcessor
studs.description: Abstract base class for processing project structures and modules. Handles project folder scanning and delegates module- or folder-specific processing to subclasses via the abstract processFolder(ProjectLayout) method. Extend this class to implement custom analysis, generation, documentation, validation, or indexing logic over detected project layouts.

examples.description: Implements a ProjectProcessor subclass to process each detected folder layout, printing its source directories.

customizations.name: projectDir
customizations.description: Sets the project root directory used by a layout and returns the same instance for fluent chaining. Concrete implementations narrow the return type (e.g., MavenProjectLayout, GradleProjectLayout, JScriptProjectLayout, DefaultProjectLayout) for convenient builder-style configuration before invoking accessors.

examples.snippet: org.machanism.machai.project.layout.MavenProjectLayout layout = new org.machanism.machai.project.layout.MavenProjectLayout().projectDir(new java.io.File("C:\\repo"));
examples.description: Fluently configures the project root directory on a MavenProjectLayout instance.

customizations.name: model
customizations.description: Sets the Maven model directly on a MavenProjectLayout instead of parsing it from pom.xml, returning the instance for chaining. Useful when the Maven model is already available in memory (e.g., from an existing Maven build context).

examples.description: Injects a preconstructed Maven Model into a MavenProjectLayout and reads the derived project identifier.

customizations.name: processFolder
customizations.description: Abstract extension point on ProjectProcessor that subclasses must implement to define custom logic for processing a detected ProjectLayout. This is the primary hook for building analysis, generation, documentation, validation, or indexing tools on top of Project Layout.

examples.description: Overrides processFolder to build a documentation scanner that reports each layout's documentation directories.

examples.title: Add Project Layout as a Maven dependency
examples.description: Declare the dependency in your project's pom.xml so tools can resolve project structure consistently.
examples.snippet:
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.machanism.machai</groupId>
  <artifactId>project-layout</artifactId>
  <version>1.3.0</version>
</dependency>

examples.title: Detect a project layout and resolve conventional directories
examples.description: Use ProjectLayoutManager to auto-detect the appropriate layout implementation for a repository root, then resolve source, test, and documentation directories without hard-coding ecosystem-specific rules.

examples.title: Build a custom project processor
examples.description: Extend ProjectProcessor and implement processFolder(ProjectLayout) to run custom logic across a project's modules, then invoke scanFolder(File) on the project root. Step 1: add the project-layout dependency. Step 2: subclass ProjectProcessor. Step 3: implement processFolder. Step 4: call scanFolder on the target directory.

examples.title: Use a specific Maven layout directly
examples.description: When the ecosystem is known, instantiate MavenProjectLayout directly, configure the project root, and query the parsed Maven model and modules.

examples.title: Read a pom.xml into a Maven model with PomReader
examples.description: Parse a pom.xml file into an org.apache.maven.model.Model, resolve properties, and serialize the model back to XML.
